# Historisk høje renter og gæld øger risikoen for aktiefald: "Jeg er bekymret"

**Feed**: borsen-podcast  
**Published**: 2026-08-19  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

This Danish investing podcast weighs cautious optimism against rising long-term US interest rates (30-year near 5.3%) and ballooning sovereign and AI-datacenter debt, which the hosts fear could trigger a large equity correction if earnings growth stalls. Stock discussion centers on cheap, buyback-heavy Danish banks (Jyske, Danske), a supercyclical Maersk that keeps rising despite an overwhelmingly bearish analyst corps, a DFDS turnaround led by Polaris, and Novo Nordisk's strategic dilemma versus Eli Lilly in the obesity/GLP-1 market. The mood is one of near-term constructiveness shadowed by explicit macro concern ('we're running over the cliff but haven't looked down yet').

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 JYSK — Jyske Bank | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 85%

Cheap (PE ~12), consistently beats, record DKK3bn buyback (~5.5% of shares), strong AM AUM growth, low risk; Jens' largest position held for years.

#### Reasoning

A predictable, low-risk compounder: rising earnings plus aggressive share cancellation acts as a 'money machine'. Trades cheap on ~12x earnings with growing asset-light asset management. Jens views it as one of the best on the exchange; Jesper adds AUM +9% is a positive leading indicator of future asset-light revenue.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the share price rises enough to make other stocks more attractive
- if an economic downturn hits Denmark and loan losses rise

> *"Vi har ett sällskap här som är stadig ett av de billiga på börsen... de köper in med armar och ben egna aktier. De är i gång med det största tillbaka-program de har haft någonsin på 3 miljarder."*

---

### 🟠 DFDS — DFDS | **WATCH** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 55%

Board shake-up: ex-CEO Smedegaard likely new chairman, Polaris took >4% stake and board seat; stock +18%. Turnaround needs freight-market recovery and years to fix Turkey/logistics.

#### Reasoning

Market cheered the leadership overhaul and Polaris' involvement, a fund with prior turnaround success. But the sprawling business (Turkey, Gibraltar, freight) can't be fixed quickly, and real upside also needs the general freight market to improve. Grimaldi competition on the Turkey-Trieste route hurts.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the extraordinary general meeting rejects the board changes
- if the freight market stays weak
- if Turkey route competition intensifies

> *"Jag tror att det är riktigt bra det man gör nu. Och jag tror att Polaris är en riktigt god partner att få med in."*

---

### ⛔ MAERSK-B — AP Moller Maersk | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Best C25 stock YTD on disruption-driven freight rates, but 16 of 27 analysts say sell; long-term ~40% capacity of newbuilds (25-yr ship life) threatens years of low freight rates.

#### Reasoning

Near-term earnings surge from Red Sea/supply-chain disruptions is unsustainable; the huge orderbook means potential years of depressed container freight rates. Jens has never felt comfortable buying it, preferring refined-product tankers (Torm). Only the growing, stable terminal/logistics business is a genuine 'gold deck'. Short-covering/low free float amplify the rally.

#### Sell Triggers

- if freight-rate disruptions normalize
- if the ~40% newbuild capacity floods the market
- if analyst downgrades finally bite

> *"Så jag vill långt, långt hellre vara inne på oljeskibet... samlet ser så är och blir märsk ett container. De kommer till att gå hårdtider i mödet."*

---

### 🟢 TRMD — Torm | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Jens holds a decent stake in refined oil-product tankers; underinvestment in newbuilds vs old ships leaving the fleet favors product tankers over containers.

#### Reasoning

Opposite dynamic to Maersk: too few newbuild product tankers relative to aging ships being scrapped, supporting rates. Jens strategically prefers refined-oil-product shipping over container freight on the long view.

#### Sell Triggers

- if a wave of product-tanker newbuilds is ordered
- if refined-product demand collapses

> *"Raffinerade oljeprodukter, där jag har en pän andel i tormen. För där är det det motsatta som gör sig kallande."*

---

### ⛔ NOVO-B — Novo Nordisk | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Klaus sold last shares Feb near bottom; not positioned due to strategic 'hole'. Strong platform but Lilly stronger; CagriSema disappointed (sales hopes cut from ~134bn to <30bn DKK).

#### Reasoning

Klaus sees no clear long-term winner case in Novo's molecule pipeline right now versus his other holdings; the portfolio risks becoming a 'basket' of undifferentiated products. Facing a stronger US competitor (Lilly) in and outside the US. Positive: van der Winkel joining board/scientific committee, possible pipeline surprises at capital markets day. Fears an aggressive value-destructive M&A pivot.

#### Sell Triggers

- if capital markets day reveals a differentiated pipeline winner
- if Novo pivots to a value-destructive volume/M&A strategy
- if CagriSema underperforms on scripts

> *"Så vi är inte positionerade i något, och det är på grund av det här strategiska, man kan säga, hull, som jag syns det är just nu."*

---

### 🟢 LLY — Eli Lilly | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Held as the obesity 'winner'; next molecule retatrutide (triple agonist) delivered strong June weight-loss data; aggressive Discovery-stage dealmaking to build next-decade pipeline.

#### Reasoning

Klaus positions Lilly as the market leader with a stronger portfolio than Novo, both in and outside the US, and a strong upcoming triple-agonist. Its aggressive licensing/Discovery strategy secures future differentiated molecules — the key to staying in 'Champions League'.

#### Sell Triggers

- if retatrutide trial or launch data disappoints
- if a competitor's molecule proves superior

> *"Vi har vinnaren, vi har Ella och Lilly, som har också ett nästa mulet kyl på väg, som heter Retostotide, som är en tribelagonist, och som har levererat riktigt flotta vägtapsdata."*

---

### 🟡 COLO-B — Coloplast | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 55%

Weak since portfolio entry (now ~332 vs bought ~432) but Q beat on many metrics; new CEO Gavin Wood focused on execution, US/chronic-care growth, halting value-destructive M&A. Stock +3%.

#### Reasoning

Turnaround thesis hinges on new CEO delivering a credible plan at the annual report (Q4); prior expensive acquisitions (Kerecis) destroyed value and hurt return on invested capital. Hosts want the shares much higher but need proof of execution and possibly a reset of growth targets before conviction. Both want to hold and see the plan.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the Q4/annual report plan disappoints
- if M&A-driven strategy continues instead of organic focus
- if margin/ROIC keeps deteriorating

> *"Det kom en regnskap i går som var på en mängd parametrar bättre än väntat. De har ju fått en ny topchef, Gavin Wood... men den ska helt klart upp."*

---

### 🟢 DANSKE — Danske Bank | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Near all-time-high, solid H1 report, best-positioned Danish bank for asset-light asset management. No re-rating left; ~10% annual return expected from earnings growth.

#### Reasoning

Jesper holds it long-term for valuation and growth drivers, especially strong asset-light asset management positioning. He cautions the multiple has re-rated, so future returns (~10%/yr) rely on earnings growth and will be lower than the 5-10yr past returns of Danske/Jyske.

#### Sell Triggers

- if earnings growth slows
- if rate cuts compress net interest income more than expected

> *"Det är en bank här hemma som är bäst positionerad inför Asset Management... det är kanske omkring 10 procent årlig avkast man kan förvänta, men inte mycket mer."*

---

### 🔴 NETC — Netcompany | **SELL** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Neutral | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 45%

Ole met the company and proposes selling 50% of the position to rotate into Samsung or hold cash.

#### Reasoning

Ole flagged a portfolio change, wants to trim after meeting management, viewing a rotation to volatile memory stocks (Samsung) as a short-term trade or raising cash amid macro caution. Speculative and not a firm conviction sell.

#### Sell Triggers

- if management outlook improves
- if Samsung rotation opportunity closes

> *"Så han frågar om det är möjligt att sälja 50% av Netcompany och Vestas och stå lite cash."*

---

### 🔴 VWS — Vestas | **SELL** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Neutral | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 40%

Ole proposes selling 50% of the position to raise cash amid macro caution.

#### Reasoning

Part of Ole's proposed de-risking to free up cash; speculative trim rather than a fundamentally argued exit.

#### Sell Triggers

- if macro risk subsides
- if wind-sector outlook improves

> *"sälja 50% av Netcompany och Vestas och stå lite cash"*

---

### 🟠 005930 — Samsung | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Neutral | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 40%

Rotation candidate from Netcompany; memory stocks ultra-volatile, jumped 4300→5000, seen as a short-lived trade; Ole waiting for a correction.

#### Reasoning

Ole sees Samsung/memory as an ultra-volatile, inherently short-term investment; after the recent spike he's waiting for a pullback before buying, so it's a watch rather than an outright buy.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the memory-cycle rolls over
- if the volatility spikes against entry

> *"Samsung och Memorystocks är ultra volatila så det blir oavsett en kortvarig investering."*

---

### 🟡 IFX — Infineon | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Bought before summer, down ~28%; fell 7-8% and characterized as 'a bit expensive'.

#### Reasoning

The position is deeply underwater and described as having been expensive, but no explicit exit call was made — offset within the portfolio by Microsoft's gains, so effectively held with negative bias.

#### Sell Triggers

- if chip-sector correction deepens
- if valuation stays stretched

> *"Jo, den har varit lite dyr. Den tog Nina Movin in lige före sommarferien och den har vi så tappt knappt 28 procent på."*

---

### 🟢 IPCO — International Petroleum | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 55%

Positive triggers: buyback program, Blackrod Canada production on stream as planned; but oil price fell on eased Iran conflict. Jesper wanted to swap Ericsson into it.

#### Reasoning

Jesper saw several positive triggers (buyback, Canadian production on stream) and considered it a good time to buy by swapping out Ericsson, but couldn't execute due to no phone signal; oil-price weakness tempered his conviction.

#### Sell Triggers

- if oil price keeps falling
- if Canadian production ramp disappoints

> *"Och deras produktion i Canada... det är kommit on stream... Så det är väldigt många positiva trigger här."*

---

### 🟡 MSFT — Microsoft | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 45%

Bought same time as Infineon, up ~35%, offsetting the Infineon loss in the portfolio.

#### Reasoning

Positive performer held in the portfolio (+35%); mentioned favorably as offsetting losses, but no fresh directional thesis beyond continued holding.

#### Sell Triggers

- if AI-capex boom rolls over
- if valuation corrects sharply

> *"Till gengäld tog hon ju Microsoft in samtidigt som vi så har la 35 procent på."*

---
